gap._description: Confirmed missing emissions (probe-verified against the real WASM)

gaps.missing: script-setup compiler macros in the TYPE-LITERAL generic form — defineProps<{ id: string }>() and defineEmits<{ (e: 'save'): void }>() — emit NO prop/event symbols. Only the runtime object/array form ({ size: Number } / ['change']) is extracted; the standard Vue 3.3+ generic form loses the entire public contract.
gaps.evidence: probe: defineProps<{ id: string }>() -> no Property symbol for id; defineEmits<{ (e: 'save'): void }>() -> no Event symbol for save (TS tree: type_arguments -> object_type -> property_signature / call_signature)
gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (vue/generic-props-emits) + mutant vue/drop-generic-macro-symbols CAUGHT (2026-08-27). The type-literal generic form defineProps<{ id: string }>() / defineEmits<{ (e: 'save'): void }>() now extracts Property/Event symbols via the type_arguments -> object_type walk (property_identifier for props, first string literal per call_signature for emits). The component's public contract is no longer lost in the standard Vue 3.3+ shape. Extension (same session, post-wave review): union literal emit types now extract EVERY member (V1b, fixture vue/generic-union-emits + mutant vue/drop-union-emit-names CAUGHT).

gaps.missing: template expressions emit NO references to the component's own members — {{ count }}, @click="onSave", :label="label", v-model="count", v-if="show" read script-side state but no Uses/references edge is emitted. The template<->script data-flow is entirely silent.
gaps.evidence: probe: {{ count }} -> only instantiates for MyButton; zero edges to count/label/onSave/show
gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (vue/template-member-uses) + mutant vue/drop-template-member-uses CAUGHT (2026-08-27). Template expressions ({{ count }}, :label, @click, v-model, v-if) now emit Uses edges (isTemplateExpression) from the component to its member symbols; identifiers are collected from interpolation raw_text and directive attribute_value, resolved only against known script members (no junk edges to intrinsics). Extension (same session, post-wave review): scope-aware — template-local bindings (v-for loop vars, slot props) shadow same-named members and are suppressed (V4, fixture vue/template-scope-shadow + mutant vue/reemit-shadowed-uses CAUGHT).

gaps.missing: duplicate contains edges — the JS/TS sub-analyzer already emits contains for script-side symbols (class -> method), and the vue analyzer's own contains pass re-emitted them, doubling every class member's containment edge in the analyzer output (the store dedupes at INSERT, but the analyzer result and any consumer of it saw 2x).
gaps.evidence: probe: <script>class Base { go() {} }</script> -> contains: Base -> go emitted TWICE (once from the sub-analyzer merge, once from the vue pass)
gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (vue/script-relations expectRelationshipCount == 1) + mutant vue/reduplicate-contains CAUGHT (2026-08-27). The vue contains pass now skips (owner, member) pairs the sub-analyzer already covered, so vue-owned members (props/emits/options) still get contains while script-side class members keep exactly one edge. Harness gained expectRelationshipCount (exact-edge pinning) so relationship duplication is a permanent gate class.

gaps.missing: scope-blind template uses — v-for loop variables (v-for="item in items") and slot props (#default="{ row }") are template-LOCAL bindings, but the V2 collector emitted Uses to them whenever a same-named script member existed. False edges: the template reads the local item/row, not the member. The TS T6 shadowed-local bug class, unguarded in the template surface.
gaps.evidence: probe: v-for="item in items" + const item = ref(...) -> uses: comp -> item emitted (FALSE); #default="{ row }" + const row = ref(...) -> uses: comp -> row emitted (FALSE)
gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (vue/template-scope-shadow forbid item/row uses) + mutant vue/reemit-shadowed-uses CAUGHT (2026-08-27). The template walk now carries a shadow scope: v-for loop vars and slot-prop destructures are registered per-subtree and suppressed from Uses collection; the v-for collection expression (items) and unshadowed members (index, rowClick) still emit.

decisions.question: style blocks (CSS) are skipped entirely — no extraction. Recommend: DECLARED LIMITATION (CSS is handled by the dedicated css analyzer; the SFC analyzer owns structure + script).
decisions.resolution: RULED — DECLARED LIMITATION (2026-08-27): style blocks are skipped entirely; CSS extraction belongs to the dedicated css analyzer, the SFC analyzer owns structure + script. Section A records style_element as handled_verified (structure) with the extraction limitation declared here.

decisions.question: v-on modifier tokens (.prevent, .stop) and dynamic directive arguments ([expr]) are structure-only — recommend INTERNAL SILENT.
decisions.resolution: RULED — INTERNAL SILENT (2026-08-27): v-on modifier tokens (.prevent, .stop) and dynamic directive arguments ([expr]) are syntax structure only; the binding VALUE expressions are covered by V2 uses. Slot-prop destructuring (#default="{ row }") is a LOCAL binding — shadowed per V4, not a member use.

decisions.question: error-recovery end-tag nodes — recommend INTERNAL SILENT (error handling).
decisions.resolution: RULED — INTERNAL SILENT (2026-08-27): erroneous_end_tag nodes are tree-sitter error-recovery artifacts; the analyzer already reports parse errors, no extraction needed.

decisions.question: typeParameters payload: the SFC component itself has no generics; script-side TS generics are handled by the TS sub-analyzer. Recommend: DECLARED N/A at the SFC level.
decisions.resolution: RULED — DECLARED N/A (2026-08-27): the SFC component itself has no generics; script-side TS generics are handled by the TS sub-analyzer. typeParameters payload row omitted from the vue Matrix (family contract).

decisions.question: apiContract payload: Vue has no framework API-contract concept (like groovy/JS) — recommend DECLARED N/A.
decisions.resolution: RULED — DECLARED N/A (2026-08-27): Vue has no framework API-contract concept (like groovy/JS); the apiContract payload row is omitted from the vue Matrix.

decisions.node_type: HTML builtin tag set drift (analyzer vs F5 oracle)
decisions.question: Can modern HTML (search) or camelCase SVG tags surface as component usages?
decisions.ruling: NO — analyzer HTML_BUILTIN_TAGS = 134 tags incl. 2023 <search> and SVG camelCase; the F5 oracle's ORACLE_HTML_TAGS carried only 126 and faked MISSING instantiates->search (Navbar.vue). Oracle extended to the identical list; the drift is now pinned by vue/modern-html-svg-builtin-tags (forbids 8 native tags) + mutant vue/reemit-filtered-kebab-tags.

decisions.question: Review H1: Vue-2 object-form data and factory return keys never became symbols, so their template refs vanished.
decisions.decision: One Property symbol per key (pair ranges; string keys unquoted) for both the object form and the first returned object of data() factories (documented approximation; nested functions not descended). Metadata isDataKey. Fixtures vue/data-keys + vue/data-factory-keys (uses controls); mutant vue/data-keys-drop.

decisions.question: Review H2: sub-analyzer errors/exports/imports pushed raw (script coordinates) while symbols pointed at SFC coordinates.
decisions.decision: Full shift helper (lines always; first-line columns; single-line end columns): scriptStartLine/Cols behavior for symbols unchanged, errors/exports/imports now share it. Fixture vue/script-error-offset pins the error line; mutant vue/error-offset-revert.

decisions.question: Review H3: ranges carried SFC lines with script-local startIndex, incoherent dimensions for every span consumer.
decisions.decision: Engine context gains sfcScriptStartIndex (block byte base, from the already-available raw_text node); the analyzer adds it to every script-derived startIndex/endIndex (absent in hand-built contexts it defaults to 0, preserving old behavior exactly). Fixture vue/range-coherence pins byte-exact ground truth via the new expectSymbolRanges gate; mutant vue/index-revert.

decisions.question: Review M1: flat tokenizing emitted every identifier, so {{ item.id }} fabricated a Uses edge to a same-named member (family receiver-only rule).
decisions.decision: Character-walk tokenizer emitting only chain roots (dot/?./#-preceded tokens skipped; shadow set still honored), no regex. Fixture vue/member-chain (uses control + forbid); mutant vue/chain-root-revert.

decisions.question: Review M2: quoted keys dropped entirely; computed [dyn] keys kept raw as unresolvable symbol names.
decisions.decision: Unquote string keys; skip bracket-led computed keys (variables, statically unknowable). Fixture vue/quoted-keys (presence + forbid); mutant vue/quoted-keys-revert covers both directions.

decisions.question: Review M3: the Vue 3 SSR hook was missing from the lifecycle list, leaving such methods invisible.
decisions.decision: One-line list addition. Fixture vue/lifecycle-server-prefetch; mutant vue/lifecycle-drop.

decisions.question: Review M4: the text-prefix check missed `export /*c*/ default`, so methods surfaced ownerless through the JS fallback (no ownerName, no Contains).
decisions.decision: Structural check (first two children are the export/default keywords, comments skipped). Fixture vue/commented-default pins ownerName; mutant vue/default-text-revert strips it.

decisions.question: Review M5 (TS-path expansion finding): Options methods/computed emitted bare signatures, the sub-analyzer versions holding parameters/returns were filtered and replaced.
decisions.decision: Index filtered method symbols by bare name and copy parameters/returnType/complexity/qualified_calls on re-emission (first wins; collisions pathological). Fixture vue/options-payload (params + returnType); mutant vue/payload-drop.

decisions.question: Deeper review D1: @click="go('save')" fabricated Uses(save) — string contents tokenized as identifiers (the old regex shared the flaw).
decisions.decision: Stack-machine tokenizer: quote states with escapes, backtick ${...} re-enters code (brace-tracked), chain-root rule preserved. Fixture vue/template-string-args (uses controls + forbid); mutant vue/string-args-revert.

decisions.question: Deeper review D2: data: () => ({...}) and data: function() {...} never reached the return-object search (method bodies only).
decisions.decision: Run the search on function-valued pair values too; direct-object rule (ancestors limited to parens/arrow/function) covers expression bodies, return rule covers blocks. Span-compared (KAD2 rule — wrapper identity never matches). Fixture vue/arrow-data; mutant vue/arrow-data-drop.

decisions.question: Deeper review D3: @Dec export default bailed on the leading decorator node, losing component ownership.
decisions.decision: Skip decorator-type leading siblings in the structural check (same treatment as comments). Fixture vue/decorated-default (ownerName pin); mutant vue/decorated-default-revert.

decisions.question: vue-element-admin MarkdownEditor deep-diff MISSING: member calls inside prop default() factory bodies (Math.random(), .toFixed(0)) emitted no calls edges. Fix the walk or verify already-fixed?
decisions.decision: RULED - VERIFIED ALREADY-FIXED at HEAD (V1/V2 embedded-script walk broadening covers the factory body): probe of the exact corpus expression emits default->toFixed + default->random; control method call (ping->helper) unchanged. Pinned by vue/prop-default-factory-calls so the contract cannot silently regress; mutant vue/prop-default-call-drop re-drops the edges and is caught.

decisions.node_type: Options-API object member duplicate keys (#745, M49 web-family dup-key ruling)
decisions.question: emitObjectMembers/emitDataKeys were first-wins (`seen.has(name)` skipped later declarations) while JS at runtime executes the LAST same-key declaration and the JS analyzer's J3 contract is last-wins — vue's graph disagreed with both runtime and its own embedded-JS sub-analyzer. Found via the web-family dup-key convergence sweep (#745).
decisions.ruling: Option A — last-wins family-wide. emitObjectMembers and emitDataKeys record the symbol index per key; a later duplicate REPLACES the earlier symbol in place (one symbol per key, keyed to the surviving LAST declaration). Pinned by fixtures/vue/dupkey-last-wins; mutant vue/dupkey-revert-first-wins dies on it.
decisions.evidence: dupkey-verify.ts (line-of surviving symbol moved first->last), F3 vue 29/29, F4 437/437

decisions.node_type: defineProps/defineEmits with a NAMED or BOUND declaration
decisions.question: F12 (master review 2026-09-30): the contract is extracted only from INLINE literals, so defineProps<AffixProps>(), defineProps(affixProps), defineEmits(binding) and the Options `props: defs` / `emits: defs` hoists emit NOTHING. Measured on the restored corpora: 103/103 defineProps<Named> sites, 67/67 defineEmits(binding), 22/22 defineProps(binding) and 14 Options `props:` sites lost the whole contract — 132 of the 232 corpus files that declare one (11.5% of the corpus). Every one is resolvable on disk (97 import the declaration from a sibling module, 6 declare it in the same file, 0 unresolvable), so this was a shape-match, not unknowability.
decisions.decision: TWO shapes, each for a measured reason. (A) A same-file BINDING resolves inside the SFC's own script trees and its object-literal keys are published by nothing else, so component-owned Property/Event symbols are emitted exactly as the inline runtime form emits them. (B) A NAMED or IMPORTED declaration is an EDGE from the component to the declaring name (metadata isPropContract / isEmitContract, plus contractModule and an `unresolved` flag), because the sub-analyzer already publishes that declaration's members under the DECLARATION's ownership and the store's SYMBOL key is ${fileId}:${name}:${startLine} with owner NOT in it — a component-owned copy at the same name and line was MEASURED to silently replace the declaration's own row. The edge is emitted AFTER the sub-analyzer merge: the store's RELATIONSHIP identity is (source, target, type, line) with no metadata component and INSERT OR IGNORE, so an edge pushed during the macro walk loses to the sub-analyzer's own type_argument row at the store. `metadata.contractSource` (inline | generic | binding) records which shape produced each symbol, so a fixture can pin the shape and a mutant can revert one without touching the others.
decisions.result: 345 of 345 corpus contract declarations now answerable, from 213 (61.7%). Fixtures vue/named-contract + vue/options-named-contract; mutants vue/named-contract-drop + vue/contract-edge-drop + vue/options-contract-binding-drop, all CAUGHT, each failing for exactly one reason. F3 vue 34/34, F4 0 vue survivors, differential 100%/0/0 on both corpora at 200-file depth, phantom census unchanged (261/2985/0).

decisions.node_type: store identity — symbol key and relationship key
decisions.question: A design constraint the F12 fix had to be built around, recorded because it constrains every lane: `brain_symbol.id` is ${fileId}:${name}:${startLine} (owner NOT in the key, insert is INSERT OR REPLACE) and `brain_relationship.id` is ${projectId}:rel:${sourceId}:${targetName}:${relType}:${line} (no metadata component, insert is INSERT OR IGNORE).
decisions.ruling: RULED, with one measured consequence and one LATENT defect. (a) Two owners of one name on one LINE cannot both be stored — PROVEN by injecting a component-owned copy of an interface member and watching the interface's own row vanish. Corpus incidence measured: ZERO across all 1,150 restored .vue files, so it is latent, not live. It is nonetheless reachable: `methods: { a() {} }, props: { a: String }` on one line is legal Vue and emits two symbols the store cannot both hold (f12-keyfamily.ts K3). No corpus file writes that shape, so a fixture pins it and the store key stays unchanged. (b) Two RELATIONSHIPS differing only in metadata are collapsed to the first — the contract marker must therefore be applied to an existing row rather than added beside it, which is why the F12 edge is emitted after the merge.

decisions.question: F12's design needed a cross-file fact (a declaration in a sibling module's members). src/ast/override-context.ts:16 and src/ast/types.ts:217 both state the production indexer provides the companion 'from its global symbol space (wired via M12.44)'. Measured: `overrideCompanion` is passed by NO production code path — only by script/m12 and script/m14 probe harnesses. The F12 fix therefore cannot lean on it.
decisions.ruling: RULED — the two comments are FALSE as written and the companion is a probe-only facility. Recorded here because it is the reason the F12 fix is a graph answer (an edge) rather than a symbol copy, and because the claim is family-wide. Two consequences owed by their owners, not by the vue lane: either wire the companion in the indexer or amend the two comments; and note that a companion is a PARTIAL view by construction (see the perl mutant `typescript/override-companion` for the failure mode an unguarded partial companion has).

decisions.question: F7 (master review 2026-09-30): `hasTypeInference: false` was HARDCODED, so every SFC reported the same value — including the 778 of 1,150 restored corpus files with a lang="ts" block, whose interface/annotation members the TypeScript analyzer extracted correctly while the flag denied it. A per-file field reported a constant.
decisions.decision: TRUE iff at least one <script> block was dispatched to a TypeScript grammar (lang="ts" or lang="tsx", #903's three-way dispatch) — the fact the pipeline already computes as `isTs`. A plain block, or an SFC with no script, is the JavaScript analyzer and stays false. BOTH directions are pinned by a fixture PAIR (vue/ts-type-inference, vue/js-type-inference) because a one-sided pin cannot see a mutant that flips the constant unconditionally — vue/type-inference-always-true is caught only by the negative half, which is the M49 T6 lesson in its metadata form.
decisions.evidence: fixtures vue/ts-type-inference + vue/js-type-inference; mutants vue/type-inference-hardcoded-false + vue/type-inference-always-true, both CAUGHT, each by exactly one fixture.

decisions.question: F1 (master review 2026-09-30, High): Options-API INHERITANCE produced no relationship of any kind. `extends:` and `mixins:` had no branch, so Vue's own class heritage was absent from the graph and the base surfaced only as a bare `uses` from the sub-analyzer. Counterfactual: the SAME text as a .ts file emits `extends: Child->BasePanel`. Corpus: `extends:` is written by 0 files, `mixins:` by 9.
decisions.decision: Both become `extends` edges from the component, distinguished by `metadata.isMixin` — Vue 2 documents `extends` as class inheritance and `mixins` as an options merge, and both make the named component's options part of this one. The RELATION was chosen deliberately: `extends` is ALREADY in this lane's audited set (M60 rel-type-coverage CHECK 1 lists it for vue), so the oracle now compares these rows instead of them sitting where no gate could see them. Three accepted name shapes: a bare identifier, an array, and a string. The inline-object form (`extends: { methods: {...} }`) is a MERGE, so it yields no base class and its members become this component's members. Confidence 0.9, not 1.0: the option is resolved by Vue at runtime, so the analyzer states the relationship without being able to see the base's members.
decisions.evidence: fixture vue/options-inheritance; mutants vue/inheritance-edge-drop + vue/mixin-label-swap, both CAUGHT, each for exactly one reason. Oracle side: deriveVueHeritageTruth in script/m14/differential.ts, derived on the EMBEDDED SCRIPT trees (the SFC tree exposes the script as one raw_text leaf, so an export_statement is not there) and reading `default` from `children` not `namedChildren` (it is an anonymous token). Truth rows on vue-element-admin moved 882 -> 891, exactly the +9 heritage rows, and they went from 9 unexplained fabrications to 0 unexplained verified rows.

decisions.question: F2 (master review 2026-09-30, High): provide()/inject() is Vue's THIRD contract leg — what a component provides and what it depends on — and had no branch. `provide(` is written by 34 corpus files, `inject(` by 45; the corpus writes ZERO Options `provide:` / `inject:` options, and all 79 call sites use an IDENTIFIER key (`provide(anchorKey, …)`, `inject(avatarGroupContextKey, undefined)`), never a string.
decisions.decision: A `references` edge from the component to the key, carrying metadata.isProvideContract or isInjectContract, confidence 0.9. The identifier key names a declaration this file does not own, so the answer is an edge, not a copy — the F12 shape for the same reason. A key that both provides and injects yields two rows with different markers, so the two halves of one key are joinable in the graph by name: element-plus steps.vue provides STEPS_INJECTION_KEY and item.vue injects it, and that pair is now visible. The keys of an inline `provide(K, { … })` value are this component's own CONTRIBUTION and are annotated onto the symbols the sub-analyzer already emitted — in place, never re-pushed, because the store's symbol key excludes owner and a second symbol at the same name and line silently replaces the first (VSD25). That annotation is what removed the 4 ownerless Method symbols the census measured on tour.vue (updateModelValue, onClose, onFinish), which were indistinguishable in the graph from module-level functions. Measured after: fires on all 72 corpus files, 39 provide + 52 inject edges, 4 symbols newly owned.
decisions.evidence: fixture vue/provide-inject-contract; mutants vue/provide-inject-edge-drop + vue/provided-owner-drop, both CAUGHT, each for exactly one reason. F3 vue 38/38, F4 40 vue mutants 0 survivors.
decisions.verification_limit: NOT verified by the differential, and the reason is structural, not incidental: the analyzer-side comparison set for vue is [extends, implements, instantiates, overrides, calls] (script/m14/differential.ts:22846), so `references` is FILTERED OUT of the comparison — along with `contains` and `uses`. F2's 91 edges, F12's contract edges, and every delegated `references` row the sub-analyzer emits are stored and compared against NOTHING. That is precisely what the M60 rel-type-coverage gate CHECK 1 reports as un-audited debt for this lane, and it is why the 100%/0% differential figure is silent about all of them. The honest statement is: these edges are fixture-gated and mutant-gated, NOT oracle-gated. Closing that gap means deriving `references` in the JavaScript oracle (shared by js/vue/svelte) and adding the label to the audited set; it is owed and is the highest-value remaining item in the lane.

decisions.question: F8 (master review 2026-09-30): a `name:` option produced a SECOND Class symbol alongside the SFC's own, and the two had DISJOINT edge sets with neither reachable as a target. Measured THROUGH THE STORE on WidgetFile.vue declaring name:'ActualName': 6 edges sourced the file stem (delegated imports/exports/uses) and 2 contained edges sourced the option name, so 'what contains lab?' answered ActualName while 'what imports from this file?' answered WidgetFile — one component, two answers, no edge to unify them. 74 of 1,150 corpus files declared a `name:` differing from the file stem.
decisions.decision: ONE component, ONE Class symbol, named by the DECLARED identity (`name:` is what `components: {}` resolves by and what devtools shows), else the file stem. The SFC symbol is RENAMED in place rather than a second one pushed — the earlier dedupe only fired when the two names were EQUAL, which is why the common case was covered and the renamed one was not. The file stem is not discarded: it is the module's identity in the import graph and is recorded in metadata.moduleName. The seam re-points every component-owned edge to the one symbol as a SINGLE sweep after all producers have run, because the template pass (step 2) emits before the script pass has read `name:` — a per-row re-point in the merge loop fixed the delegated rows and left every template `instantiates` on the file stem, which the fixture caught immediately.
decisions.result: 0 of 1,150 corpus files now carry two Class symbols (was 74); 89 are renamed by a `name:` option, each with one symbol and metadata.moduleName; 0 edges with an unresolvable source. SIDE EFFECT worth recording: the phantom-name census fell from 261 to 211, because the component symbol is now named by something the file actually WRITES rather than by its own stem. Differential 100%/MISSING=0/unexplained=0 on both corpora.
decisions.evidence: fixture vue/options-rename-identity; mutants vue/component-split-identity + vue/identity-edge-source-unrepointed, both CAUGHT. The second is caught ONLY by the four `from: ActualName` relationship rows plus their four mirrored forbid rows — a symbol-count assertion cannot see the edge half, which is why the fixture pins both.

decisions.question: F10 (master review 2026-09-30): an UNQUOTED object-literal key in a template expression read as a component member — `{{ { count: 1 } }}` emitted Uses(count) when nothing in that expression reads the member. Measured at 432 of 1,150 restored corpus files (37.6%). The QUOTED form was already correct: the stack tokenizer skipped string CONTENTS and never modelled the key POSITION, which the in-file comment acknowledged as a pre-existing acceptance rather than solving.
decisions.decision: An identifier is a key when it is followed (modulo whitespace) by a single `:` AND no pending ternary `?` is open AT THAT BRACE DEPTH. The pending `?` is tracked per depth because `c ? { p: 1 } : d` opens the `?` at the outer depth and the key colon at the inner one, and conflating them either resurrects the key or deletes the value. `?.` and `??` do not open a ternary, and a ternary colon consumes the marker. Shorthand `{ height }` and `{ height: height }` both remain READS — the first has no colon, the second's value does — and shorthand `{ height: height }` is why 26 corpus edges remain and are CORRECT.
decisions.verification_note: Two fixtures, because a forbid-only fixture would have scored the wrong fix as a pass. vue/template-object-key declares count/label as REAL members that appear ONLY as keys — the defect only manifests when a member of that name exists, so a fixture that omitted them can never fail, and the mutant that restores the defect SURVIVED the first version of that fixture. vue/template-ternary-value pins the three positions the naive rule breaks: the VALUE side of a ternary, the value alongside a key, and the CONTENT of a computed key `[count]` (which names no property, so it is a real read). `from` in both is the component's declared `name:`, not the file stem — since F8 the one Class symbol is named by `name:`, and a forbid row written against the stem matches nothing and reads as green for the wrong reason.
decisions.result: 432 corpus files -> 0 residual defects. The 26 surviving key-shaped targets are shorthand properties, all verified by hand against their source lines.
decisions.evidence: fixtures vue/template-object-key + vue/template-ternary-value; mutants vue/template-object-key-revert + vue/template-ternary-value-drop, both CAUGHT. The second is the FALSE NEGATIVE the fix exists to avoid and is caught only by the ternary fixture's require rows.

decisions.node_type: references — the audited set (family, not vue-only)
decisions.question: F12 and F2's contract edges were fixture-gated and mutant-gated but NOT oracle-gated: the analyzer-side comparison set for vue is [extends, implements, instantiates, overrides, calls] (differential.ts), so `references` was filtered out of the comparison entirely — as were `contains` and `uses`. The M60 rel-type-coverage gate CHECK 1 reports this as un-audited debt. Closing it means deriving `references` in the oracle.
decisions.decision: DERIVED SCOPED, and the audited set made METADATA-AWARE. Measured first: `references` has NINE producers in this lane over 531 corpus files — ~1,664 sub-analyzer local reads (a `line` metadata key, no relationshipType), 511 declared_type, 377 type_argument, 177 cast_target, 19 type_alias, 6 instanceof_check, 1 satisfies_target, plus the 217 F12 contract and 95 F2 provide/inject rows. Deriving the whole label means re-implementing two analyzers' type-reference and identifier-read extraction inside the differential — a project, not a task. So `deriveVueContractEdges` derives ONLY the compiler-contract family and `VUE_CONTRACT_ROW` admits ONLY rows carrying a contract marker, which sizes the claim to what is checked and leaves the other ~2,750 rows as declared debt the rel-type-coverage gate keeps reporting. Adding the BARE label would have compared 2,750 rows against nothing and reported each as a fabrication — which is how a partial derivation becomes a dishonest gate.
decisions.result: MISSING 79 -> 0 and coverage 100% on BOTH corpora at 200-file depth, with the 312 contract rows this wave introduced now genuinely audited. RESIDUAL, open and precisely located: 3 analyzer rows on element-plus remain unexplained (ElDropdownItem -> dropdownItemProps, ElSelectV2 -> selectV2Props, ElSelectV2 -> selectV2Emits) — the OPTIONS hoist `props: defs` / `emits: defs`, which the derivation does not yet read. The fix is written and has been lost four times to a concurrent rewrite of differential.ts; it is not landed.
decisions.harness_bug_found: The allowance is evaluated on the NORMALIZED analyzer row, and the normalization DROPPED `metadata`, so VUE_CONTRACT_ROW could never fire and the analyzer's rows were filtered out while the oracle emitted the same rows as truth. Carrying metadata fixes it. This is the M60/#910 note reproduced 90 lines below its own warning: 'measured 129 MISSING ... the change would have read as an analyzer regression when it was a harness gap.'
decisions.instrument_gap_found: The summary printed samples ONLY for MISSING and ONLY when MISSING was non-zero, so a lane at MISSING=0 / unexplained=3 — exactly the state this landed in — reported a residual with no way to see it. Both directions now print, each labelled. A count you cannot triage is the same failure class as this lane's whole review.

decisions.node_type: regex inventory (the census is a published claim)
decisions.question: The docs said the analyzer holds 0 regex usages and its own file header said "fully regex-free", while the census registers 6. Which is true?
decisions.decision: The CENSUS was right and both prose claims were false. Corrected in docs/analyzers/real-vue-analyzer.md (with each literal's class and justification, and its line number) and in the file header, which now says NOT regex-free and points at the register. A 7th literal was considered and REJECTED during F9: the dotted tag name is recovered with indexOf/charCodeAt rather than a new pattern, because the grammar already hands the spelling over in two pieces.
decisions.measurement: Live scan of the file: 6 literals, unchanged in count by this wave, at lines 50 / 437 / 2099 / 2111 / 2125 / 2127 (previously published as 45 / 314 / 1091 / 1103 / 1117 / 1119 — the numbers drifted because the fixes added code, which is exactly why the census is the authority and the doc records them as locators, not keys). `/src/m` is a URL in a source-map comment, not a pattern.
decisions.evidence: validation/m49/regex-debt-register.json; docs/analyzers/real-vue-analyzer.md regex section; vue/decorator-metadata-868

decisions.node_type: computed object keys (M2 / VSD15 applied to one site of four)
decisions.question: The ruling "a bracket-led computed key names a variable, so skip it" was implemented in `emitObjectMembers` and nowhere else, though four sites turn an object key into a symbol name. Is the ruling wrong, or under-applied?
decisions.decision: UNDER-APPLIED, and the ruling itself is right. `emitDataKeys`, `propEntries` and `genericMacroEntries` each lacked the guard, and `genericMacroEntries` additionally walked INDEX SIGNATURES as if they were members. Each site now carries the same one-line guard. SCOPE, recorded because it is cross-lane and not this lane's to change: an index signature in a STANDALONE `interface` in the script is the TypeScript delegate's own deliberately-marked emission (metadata.isIndexSignature + indexParameter, real-typescript-analyzer.ts:3610) — the vue fix is the INLINE type-literal path, which vue does own.
decisions.measurement: Corpus: the one real phantom was `Property "[key]"` at panel-date-pick.vue:846. After the fix, 0 vue-owned bracket-led phantoms across 1,139 files; the 2 that remain are both the delegate's marked index signature. Not cosmetic: the store's symbol key is name+line, so a phantom can also DISPLACE a real member.
decisions.evidence: vue/computed-key-guard (plain / plainProp / save / plainInline are the controls a whole-bracket guard would lose); vue/computed-key-guard-drop

decisions.question: `data`, the lifecycle hooks, `methods`, `computed` and `watch` all became Methods. `setup` — the function an Options component is built around — was in none of them.
decisions.decision: CLOSED with its OWN branch and its own `isSetup` marker, deliberately NOT folded into `isLifecycleHook`: it is the composition entry point, not a lifecycle hook, and merging the two would make that predicate's name lie for every other caller.
decisions.measurement: 20 element-plus files gained a `setup` Method (0 before). The vue-element-admin occurrence (`Tinymce/index.vue:146`, `setup(editor)`) is a NESTED Tinymce plugin callback at 8-space indent, not a root-component setup, and the root-options walk correctly excludes it — an earlier survey count of 21 included it, so 20 is the corrected figure.
decisions.evidence: vue/options-setup-method; vue/options-setup-method-drop

decisions.question: Two component-usage defects, both LATENT on the restored corpora (0 occurrences in 1,139 files) and both proven by probe against production parseFile.
decisions.decision: BOTH CLOSED. (a) A known builtin NAMESPACE (`svg`, `math`, `mathml`, `xlink`, `html`, `xhtml`) means markup, so the tag is not a usage; an UNKNOWN namespace is still reported, so the rule fails toward visibility rather than silence — deliberately not a blanket "contains a colon" rule. (b) `tag_name` spells only the ROOT segment of a dotted tag, so `<Form.Input/>` recorded `instantiates -> Form` and lost the leaf. The target stays `Form` — the name the components registry holds and a resolver must match — and the leaf rides in metadata (`member`, `componentPath`), which is lossless without inventing an unresolvable `Form.Input` symbol. The spelling is read from the `start_tag` TEXT: `tagNameNode.parent` is the `element` node, so its text starts with `<` and produced targets like `<div` (measured, broke five fixtures before it was corrected).
decisions.measurement: Probe before fix: `<svg:circle/>` -> `instantiates -> svg:circle`; `<Form.Input/>` -> `instantiates -> Form`. After: builtins excluded, `Form`/`Ui` carry `member: Input` / `member: Table`, and `<div>` `<span>` `<template>` are unaffected.
decisions.evidence: vue/tag-namespace-and-dotted (forbid rows cover `svg`, `math:mi`, `svg:circle` AND `Form.Input`, so suppressing only known strings still fails); vue/namespaced-builtin-false-positive; vue/dotted-tag-leaf-drop

decisions.question: The macro handler reads the inner `defineProps` call and never looked one frame UP at the `withDefaults` wrapping it. The documented way to give a typed prop a default lost every default.
decisions.decision: CLOSED on BOTH resolutions, because 100% of the corpus is the NAMED form and a fix on only the symbol path would have changed nothing observable. Component-owned prop symbols (inline type literal, same-file binding) take `metadata.defaultValue` as WRITTEN SOURCE — this lane has no evaluator and storing text beats pretending otherwise. The NAMED form has no prop symbol to hang a default on (the members belong to the imported declaration), so the map rides the CONTRACT EDGE as `defaults` plus a `defaultKeys` COUNT, since a graph answer needs to know the contract HAS defaults, not just that one key matched. An INDIRECT argument (an imported identifier or a call) is stored as `defaultsExpression` and deliberately NOT as `defaultKeys: 0` — zero keys would assert the opposite of the truth, and the difference between "no defaults" and "defaults, elsewhere" is the whole point.
decisions.measurement: 98 of 98 corpus files now yield defaults: 446 literal keys across 82 files, 16 indirect expressions (all imported from a sibling module, so resolving the VALUES would be cross-file constant folding this lane does not do). 0 misses, against 0 recovered before the fix.
decisions.evidence: vue/with-defaults-propagation (all three resolutions plus the indirect and call-wrapped shapes); vue/with-defaults-drop (reverts BOTH paths in one mutant, because a fixture pinning only `defaultValue` would be satisfied by a fix that wired the symbol path and skipped the edge)

decisions.node_type: identifier elements of a macro ARRAY — `defineEmits([CHANGE_EVENT, …])`
decisions.question: `propEntries` accepted string elements only, so an IDENTIFIER element — which names a declaration, not an event — was dropped with no symbol AND no edge. Found by the gate, not by review: the 829-file draw reported it as MISSING rows (`time-select -> CHANGE_EVENT`, `picker -> UPDATE_MODEL_EVENT`).
decisions.decision: CLOSED as a CONTRACT EDGE, the same rule `defineProps(binding)` already used: the DECLARATION is nameable here even though its VALUE is not (those constants are imported). It is a SEPARATE accessor rather than a flag on `propEntries`, so the Options-API path — which uses the same helper for `emits: [ … ]` — keeps ignoring identifiers instead of inheriting a declaration edge it never asked for, and a symbol for `CHANGE_EVENT` would be the VSD34 phantom class again.
decisions.measurement: 6 corpus files with an identifier inside a macro array, 11 contract rows. Before: time-select.vue published events `['blur','focus','clear']` where the component emits five, and referenced neither constant.
decisions.evidence: vue/declare-emits-identifier-array; vue/declare-emits-identifier-array-drop

decisions.node_type: what counts as a CONTRACT PARTICIPANT in `defineProps<…>()`
decisions.question: The rule was "walk to the first `type_identifier` ANYWHERE in the type arguments", which descends into the object literal's property signatures — and a PROPERTY'S TYPE is not a participant. Also `genericMacroEntries` read a DIRECT `object_type` child, which an INTERSECTION does not have, so `defineProps<{ … } & Pick<X, 'a'>>()` published NO props at all.
decisions.decision: CLOSED with one shape rule, mirrored in the oracle: descend INTERSECTION / UNION constituents and type wrappers, read a GENERIC's OWN name, and STOP at an object literal — its members are the props, and their types belong to the props (the delegate already publishes them as declared_type rows). A generic's type ARGUMENTS are not descended into, so `defineProps<SegmentedProps<T>>()` names `SegmentedProps` and not the component's own type parameter — the case an earlier fix had already patched by hand, now stated as a rule. Participants are emitted INDEPENDENTLY of prop symbols: an intersection carries both a literal operand and a named one, and gating the contract edge on `entries.length === 0` meant that fixing the literal silently stripped the declaration (caught by vue/options-named-contract).
decisions.measurement: 829-file draw: node.vue's `defineProps<{ node: NodeShape; menuId?: string }>()` — MISSING on the oracle side, because `NodeShape` is one prop's type and there is no participant; menu.vue's `defineProps<{ nodes: NodeShape[] } & Pick<CommonProps, 'height'>>()` — the analyzer took `CascaderNode` and the oracle took `Pick`, so each side manufactured half of one disagreement (1 unexplained + 1 MISSING on the same line). After: menu.vue emits prop symbols `['nodes','index']` (was `[]`) and the contract row `menu -> Pick` (was `menu -> CascaderNode`). 1 corpus file carries a balanced intersection.
decisions.evidence: vue/contract-type-participant; vue/contract-participant-nested-prop-type; vue/intersection-props-drop

decisions.node_type: the `defineComponent({ … })` blind spot in BOTH oracles
decisions.question: `export default { … }` and `export default defineComponent({ … })` are the two ways a Vue component is written, and both `deriveVueContractEdges` and `deriveVueHeritageTruth` read the options object as a DIRECT named child of the `export_statement` — so only the first shape was visible.
decisions.decision: CLOSED with one shared `vueDefaultOptionsObject` helper that unwraps the call's first argument. Worth stating plainly rather than filing as a routine fix: the F1 heritage oracle was NARROWER than the analyzer it was checking, and passing on vue-element-admin only showed that corpus happens to use the shape the oracle could see. The differential earned this rather than the analyzer losing rows — the analyzer was right and the oracle could not express it.
decisions.measurement: Left 3 analyzer rows unexplained on element-plus (ElDropdownItem -> dropdownItemProps, ElSelectV2 -> selectV2Props, ElSelectV2 -> selectV2Emits — all Options `props:`/`emits:` hoists inside `defineComponent`), and silently disabled heritage derivation for every defineComponent file. Both corpora: MISSING=0 / unexplained=0 after.
decisions.evidence: script/m14/differential.ts `vueDefaultOptionsObject`; vue-differential full draw

decisions.question: `override-context.ts` and `types.ts` both claimed the production indexer provides the companion index "via M12.44". Does it?
decisions.decision: NO, and the comments were corrected rather than the gap being closed, because closing it is the batch indexer's job and a comment fix is what the evidence supports. WHAT IS TRUE: the field is accepted on `AnalyzeContext`, forwarded by `pool-worker.parseFile`, and populated on demand by `override-companion-pass.ts` (PERL-MR15). WHAT IS FALSE: the BATCH indexer never builds one, so a normal full-project index run resolves every override through the deterministic first-parent fallback and the project-level answer is unreachable in that path. Separately, and not this lane's to fix: the Python analyzer reads `(ctx as any)._overrideCompanion`, a channel nothing populates.
decisions.measurement: grep for a construction site outside `override-companion-pass.ts` and the analyzers: none. 8 analyzers CONSUME the field, so the gap changes their behaviour on every batch run rather than being inert.
decisions.evidence: src/ast/override-context.ts; src/ast/types.ts; src/ast/override-companion-pass.ts (already honest about this)

decisions.node_type: store boundary — brain_relationship identity vs contract metadata
decisions.question: The analyzer emitted a correct contract row carrying `isPropContract`, `unresolved` and F3's whole `defaults` map, and NONE of it reached the graph. Which side is wrong?
decisions.decision: NEITHER, in the sense that both were correct in isolation and the STORE's relationship identity is a deliberate constraint (VSD25): `brain_relationship.id = projectId:rel:source:target:type:line` with no metadata component, inserted `INSERT OR IGNORE`. The sub-analyzer's `type_argument` row and this lane's contract row describe ONE declaration on ONE line, so they collide, the delegate is inserted first, and the POORER row wins the insert with no signal that anything was dropped. The fix is to MERGE instead of push: match on target + type + line — deliberately NOT on source — and re-attribute the merged row to the component. Re-attributing is what makes the merged row answer 'what does this component declare?' at all, since without it the row still points at whatever enclosing scope the delegate named.
decisions.measurement: Store round-trip, never before performed for this lane: with-defaults-propagation.vue kept 1 of 2 contract rows, losing `isPropContract`, `unresolved` and `defaults` entirely; skeleton-item.vue survived only because its two rows happened to differ in source. After the merge, 4 of 4 contract rows persist with markers, resolved sources, and 3 `defaults` maps. TWO wrong turns are recorded because both looked correct: comparing `c.line - c.lineOffset` against the row's line (c.line is ALREADY offset, so 113 was compared to 27 and the merge never fired), and including source in the match (the delegate sources its row at the enclosing scope, which is the component for a top-level call but the local `const props = withDefaults(…)` binding when the macro is assigned, as in menu.vue — so `menu -> Pick` still lost while the fixture file looked fixed).
decisions.evidence: script/m60/verify-vue-store-roundtrip.ts — the ONLY gate that can see this class of defect, and the reason it exists as a separate script: every other gate in this lane reads the analyzer's output, where the pre-fix and post-fix results differ only in WHICH of two equivalent rows carries the marker. An analyzer-output assertion PASSES on the broken build. It also asserts F3's `defaultKeys` agrees with the stored `defaults` map, that an indirect `defaultsExpression` does NOT claim `defaultKeys: 0` (which would assert no defaults), that F5's `setup` survives as a symbol AND a `contains` target, and that no vue-owned bracket-led phantom symbol reaches the store. Unresolved TARGETS are expected in a 4-file project and are not asserted against.

decisions.question: The register existed to make an accurate census survivable. Should Vue's 6 patterns be re-registered, justified, and carried as debt — or deleted?
decisions.decision: DELETED, all six, so the lane's own header claim is true rather than caveated. A registered pattern is still a pattern; the register makes an unavoidable pattern survivable and is the wrong instrument for six that were not unavoidable. (a) the case-insensitive line test became toLowerCase().includes; (b) quote stripping on a `name:` value became the file's existing unquote; (c) the identifier character class, used in TWO places while a hand-written tokenizer for the SAME input sat one method away, became ONE shared tokenizer — so the lane also stops having two tokenizers that disagree on method; (d,e) the two v-for patterns became `parseVForDirective`. The m49 register rows were RETIRED with a `closedByRemoval` record and the census artifact's vue rows removed with a `retired` record; no other lane's counts were touched.
decisions.measurement: Zero literals at HEAD. The v-for replacement is provably equivalent to the removed patterns over 788 generated shapes (0 diffs), and output is byte-for-byte identical over all 1,139 corpus files (25,028 relationships, 7,078 symbols). ONE REAL BUG was caught on the way: the first hand-written parser consumed the separator greedily instead of BACKTRACKING, so `v-for="item in  "` reported no collection where the regex reported one — differing on 170 of 799 shapes while ALL 47 fixtures still passed. That is the entire argument for the sweep being a gate rather than a note.
decisions.evidence: script/m60/verify-vue-no-regex.ts (counts the literals AND re-derives the equivalence every run); vue/v-for-directive-shapes; vue/component-name-double-quotes; vue/v-for-collection-backtrack-drop; vue/v-for-greedy-head-revert

decisions.node_type: performance (the axis the previous wave skipped)
decisions.question: Perf was in the requested review scope and had never been measured for this lane. Where does the time actually go, and is any of it ours?
decisions.decision: MEASURED, then fixed the two genuine defects found. Wall clock is NOT trustworthy on this host (load average 5.9-6.7, 43% swing across identical runs), so every claim below is a DETERMINISTIC count. (1) `importModuleFor` and `hasTopLevelDeclaration` each walked the ENTIRE script tree — descending into every function body — once per contract candidate: imports can only be top-level statements and a predicate named 'top level' can only look at top-level declarations, so both are now `program`'s direct children. (2) The last caller of `findDescendantType` was a branch F13 had already made DEAD, and it was the final user of a WASM descendant search on the hot path; deleted. (3) The TS delegate — which Vue's `lang=ts`/`tsx` blocks go through — recomputed `inDecoratorPosition` by climbing `.parent` per node, and web-tree-sitter implements `.parent` as a descendant search, making it O(n x depth); the flag is now threaded through the existing recursion. That change is in another lane's file and is defended by a byte-for-byte output comparison, not by reasoning.
decisions.measurement: Node visits on the 166 macro-using corpus files: 67,425 -> 8,812, i.e. 86.9% fewer / 7.7x, measured by instrumenting the real lookup. Profile: `ts_node_child_with_descendant` 5.2% -> 3.6%, vue `analyze` self time 89ms -> 61ms. Throughput ~116 -> ~128 files/s median. The TS change is proven behaviour-preserving: 400 files, 26,599 relationships, byte-identical. What remains is dominated by tree-sitter parse + WASM node marshalling (`marshalNode` 9.8%), which is shared infrastructure, not this lane.
decisions.evidence: bun --cpu-prof over the production ASTEngine.parseFile path; script/m14/tmp/vue-mr/harness.ts; TS regression net: 85/85 fixtures and 66 mutants unchanged

decisions.node_type: contains — the surface a graph is navigated by
decisions.question: `contains` had NO independent truth for this lane at any corpus scale, so a member attributed to the wrong container could not be caught once. Can it be audited?
decisions.decision: YES, for the DELEGATED half, by applying the lane-owned `oracles/typescript-contains.ts` to the embedded script trees — which is exactly what that file's header invites ('wiring it in later is one import and one registration'). Admission is PER ROW via `metadata.sfcDelegated`, not a label list and not a per-file key set, for two measured reasons. The Vue analyzer's OWN component-ownership half is NOT wired: `oracles/vue-contains.ts` now exists and covers 59 of 163 component-owned rows, and adding it half-derived would manufacture MISSING rather than audit anything. The gap is recorded here, not hidden.
decisions.measurement: Full 829-file element-plus draw: audited truth 5,938 -> 6,227 rows, still 100% covered, MISSING=0, unexplained=0; analyzer edges 5,925 -> 6,213. On the 400-file m60 draw that is the 216 delegated rows of 363 total `contains`, i.e. the label moves from wholly unaudited to 60% audited with zero fabricated green.
decisions.evidence: script/m14/oracles/vue-contains.ts; the `VUE_DELEGATED_CONTAINS_ROW` gate in differential.ts. TWO harness bugs were found and fixed while wiring it, both of which read as analyzer regressions: (1) a per-file set of the oracle's pairs was placed where the truth is derived, but the analyzer-side allowlist is evaluated in a block shared by every language AFTER the per-file loop, so it held only the LAST file's pairs — 82 MISSING on element-plus, every one demonstrably emitted by the analyzer; (2) the gate then read `r.type`, while the normalized row renames the relationship type to `label` and omits `type` entirely, so it compared `undefined` to "contains" and admitted nothing — visible as truth +82 with analyzer edges unchanged at 1487.

decisions.node_type: unknown symbols — names written nowhere in their own file
decisions.question: The m60 surface audit reported 125 symbols whose name appears nowhere in its own source. Are they defects?
decisions.decision: NO — they are names BY CONTRACT, and the fix is to DECLARE them, not to suppress them. 124 were the Vue component identity falling back to the file stem when no `name:` option is declared (F8's documented rule; the file never spells its own name), and 1 was the TypeScript delegate's invented `[key]` index-signature name. The audit already ships a GENERAL mechanism for this — `metadata.synthesized` — and its header is explicit that a declared flag cuts the other way from a name allowlist, because an UNDECLARED synthesized name still fails both rows. So the declaration was made where the rule is owned: the Vue analyzer marks the stem fallback once every script block has been read (a block carrying `name:` has already renamed the Class by then, so 'still named moduleName' IS the test), and the TypeScript analyzer marks its own invented index-signature name. No allowlist was added, and no finding was suppressed.
decisions.measurement: m60 surface audit, 400-file draw: `names not a name / not in source` 124+1 -> 0. The correctly-classified `contract literals (named by contract, not by source spelling)` channel went 0 -> 481, i.e. the findings MOVED to the disclosed channel rather than disappearing. ghost targets 0, seam keys 0, parse errors 0.
decisions.evidence: src/ast/real-vue-analyzer.ts (identityFromFileStem, declared after the block loop because the decision is only final there); src/ast/real-typescript-analyzer.ts index-signature symbol. TS regression net unchanged: 85/85 fixtures, 66 mutants.

decisions.node_type: defineOptions({ name }) — the `<script setup>` component identity
decisions.question: A `<script setup>` component declares its name with `defineOptions({ name: 'X' })` since Vue 3.3. Is that name read?
decisions.decision: NO, and that is a defect in the same class F8 fixed from the other side. `defineOptions` was present in VUE_COMPILER_MACROS only so that its CALL edge would be filtered, and nothing ever looked inside it, so a component written the modern way fell back to the FILE STEM as its identity while the file plainly declares otherwise. F8 unified the component identity but read `name:` only out of a `defineComponent({ … })` default export. The macro's `name` is now read, and because the decision arrives after the Options path has already run, the fix RE-POINTS the component's owned symbols and every edge that sourced the old identity — a bare rename would orphan exactly the members F8 worked to attach.
decisions.measurement: element-plus/table/src/table-body/td-wrapper.vue declares `name: 'TableTdWrapper'` and was published as `td-wrapper`; splitter/src/split-bar.vue declares `name: 'ElSplitterBar'` and was published as `split-bar`. After the fix both are published under their declared names, and the vue-owned `contains` oracle's agreement rose from 106/163 to 141/163. It is not cosmetic: the store's symbol key is name+line, so the declared name and the published one were two different symbols and a query for the declared name found nothing.
decisions.evidence: vue/define-options-name (the `size` prop is declared with the inline generic form precisely so the fixture fails on OWNERSHIP as well as on the name, which is what separates a rename with a re-point from a bare rename); vue/define-options-name-drop. FOUND BY THE ORACLE, not by reading: the contains oracle disagreed with the analyzer in a direction that pointed at the analyzer.

decisions.node_type: the vue-owned `contains` half — wired, or left?
decisions.question: `contains` is now audited for the DELEGATED half. The component-ownership half has an oracle at 141/163. Should it be wired?
decisions.decision: NOT WIRED, deliberately. Adding it at 141/163 would manufacture MISSING and unexplained rows rather than audit anything — the exact partial-derivation dishonesty VSD32 refused for `references`, and the reason the two halves were scoped separately. The oracle is kept as a measured asset with its gaps enumerated so the next iteration starts from data instead of from zero: it still misses `provide(key, { … })` members (F2's ownership rule, which is what `tour.vue`'s `onClose`/`onFinish`/`updateModelValue` are) and it derives `setup` for two components the analyzer does not. 147 component-owned rows remain unaudited and are counted as such.
decisions.measurement: 141/163 component-owned rows covered on a 250-file draw across both corpora; 216 of 363 total `contains` audited via the delegated TypeScript oracle (99/99 match).
decisions.evidence: script/m14/oracles/vue-contains.ts (lane-owned, with the three corrections it needed: scope option pairs to the default-export object, read `setup` as a `method_definition`, and read inline macro forms); VSD45 for the two harness bugs found while wiring.
